subject: Re: Orbit Retail hosted API renewal — capacity upsell + tier-rate redesign
messages:
From: Marcus Lin <marcus.lin@redwood.com>
To: Sophie Grant <sophie@orbitretail.com>
Cc: Naomi Feldman <naomi.feldman@redwood.com>
Date: 2026-11-13T09:12:00-08:00
Subject: Hosted API renewal discussion — proposed capacity uplift and new rate tiers

Hi Sophie,

Thanks again for the time yesterday. As discussed, Orbit's usage pattern for Q1 shows a clear upward shift in sustained token volume and peak bursts around promotional events. To make sure you don't hit soft-throttles mid-promotion, attached is a clean draft that converts your annual commit into a stepped monthly commit with a 25% burst pocket and an adjusted rate ladder that reduces per-token cost at higher tier thresholds.

Key highlights in the attached draft (OrbitRenewal_Draft_v1.pdf):
- Monthly committed units moved from 1.2B -> 1.6B tokens (phased over 3 months)
- Tiered unit pricing: discounted bands at 1.6B and 2.4B thresholds
- Burst window: +25% monthly capacity with soft-throttle grace for 48 hours
- Ops: automatic fallback to a quantized variant for non-latency-critical routes to control spend

Two asks from our side to keep the timeline tight:
1) Can procurement confirm whether Orbit can accept a one-page amendment + PO (we can DocuSign the amendment) by Nov 20?
2) If legal wants to redline, please loop them in early — we can fast-track the SLA clause around latency and fallback.

I cc'd Naomi from Renewals for billing cadence and Karthik from Infrastructure for any latency/SLO clarifications. Happy to jump on a 30-min call tomorrow if useful.

Best,
Marcus
Account Executive, Redwood Inference
m: +1 415-555-0172
attachments: OrbitRenewal_Draft_v1.pdf, capacity-forecast-2027.xlsx

Thanks Marcus — appreciate the quick follow up and draft. A few quick clarifications before we pull procurement/legal in: 

1) Burst window: Does the +25% apply as a monthly rolling buffer or only on the 48-hour promotional bursts you mentioned? We run many small promos — want to avoid unexpected throttles on those.
2) Pricing bands: Can you confirm the per-token price for the middle band (1.6B–2.4B) and whether embeddings are billed differently?
3) Data handling: Our security team will want the usual confirmation that we can pin model versions and that fallbacks do not send data to different regions.

We can do a short call tomorrow afternoon. Ben (procurement) is cc'd — Ben, do you prefer tracked PO or a blanket amendment + PO?

Best,
Sophie Grant
Head of Product, Orbit Retail

From: Karthik Iyer <karthik.iyer@redwood.com>

Subject: Re: Hosted API renewal discussion — proposed capacity uplift and new rate tiers

Hi Sophie — quick technical note from infra: 

- Burst semantics: the +25% is implemented as a monthly burst bucket with a 48-hour per-occurrence escape window. Practically that means small promos that last a few hours will consume the burst pool; recurring small promos cumulatively draw from the monthly bucket. If Orbit needs multiple guaranteed short bursts, we can propose an additional reserved micro-burst allocation (separate line item).
- Quantized fallback: fallback to quantized variants is opt-in per route. We will not shift real-time low-latency checkout routes to quantized models unless Orbit explicitly approves; default fallback routes are non-checkout, low-latency-insensitive endpoints (recommendation: cart-suggestions, search-rewrite).
- Region binding: we support model pinning per environment. Fallbacks will remain in the same region unless you ask us to route to a different regional pool.

If helpful I can join tomorrow's call to walk through the ops side.

-Karthik
Sr. Infra Engineer, Redwood Inference

Thanks — we reviewed the draft with finance. A couple procurement questions before we sign: 

- Can Redwood provide a short amortization schedule showing the monthly committed units and price per unit (so we can forecast cost and include in our Q1 budget)?
- Where does the burst usage show on invoices (line item vs aggregate)?
- We'd prefer a single amendment with an attached PO. Legal will likely redline the SLA section — can Redwood accept comments inline in DocuSign?

If those answers are straightforward, we should be able to get a PO to you by EOD Nov 20.

Ben

Ben / Sophie — great, thanks. I attached a one-page amortization export (see capacity-forecast-2027.xlsx) that maps committed units to monthly billing and shows projected burst consumption under the 25% model. Quick answers inline here: 

- Amortization: spreadsheet tab 'Amortization' shows monthly committed units and effective per-token cost by band. We can generate a PDF if you prefer for procurement.
- Invoice line items: burst consumption appears as a separate line item called 'Burst Adjustment' with monthly reconciliation — we can also show a running usage ledger on the Console for each invoice period.
- DocuSign/redlines: yes — we accept inline comments in DocuSign and will turn around small redlines within 48 hours. For any material SLA changes, legal will flag and we'll route to our GC.

Next steps I propose: 
1) I'll upload the amendment to DocuSign and invite Ben (you) by EOD Nov 20.
2) Naomi will issue a pro-forma invoice for your finance team.
3) Karthik and I can run a 20-min ops handoff the week of Nov 22 to pin routes and confirm fallback opt-ins.

If that timeline works, flag and I'll kick off the DocuSign.

Thanks,
Marcus
Account Executive, Redwood Inference
